messages.content: I would like to find a movie to watch in the Imaginative fiction genre, as I have started to watch a lot of fantasy-type movies lately, you know!!!!!!

function.name: Movies_3_FindMovies
function.description: Retrieves a list of movies based on the director, genre, and cast specified by the user. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directed_by.description: Director of the movie. Use 'dontcare' if the director is not a specific search criterion.

genre.description: Genre of the movie. Use 'dontcare' to include all genres or genre is not specified by user

cast.description: Names of leading actors or actresses in the movie. Use 'dontcare' if the cast is not a specific search criterion.

message.reasoning: User wants a movie in "Imaginative fiction" genre. The function expects genre options: "Offbeat" | "Fantasy" | "World" | "Mystery" | "Thriller" | "Comedy" | "Comedy-drama" | "Horror" | "Animation" | "Sci-fi" | "Cult" | "Drama" | "Anime" | "Family" | "Action" | "dontcare". There's no "Imaginative fiction" option. We need to interpret. The user says "Imaginative fiction genre" but we only have "Fantasy" maybe. So we can ask clarifying question or choose "Fantasy". The user also says they have started to watch a lot of fantasy-type movies. So likely they want a fantasy movie. We can ask them if they'd like a fantasy movie. But we can also interpret "Imaginative fiction" as "Fantasy". The best approach: ask clarifying question: "Do you mean fantasy?" Or we can proceed with "Fantasy". The user says "as I have started to watch a lot of fantasy-type movies lately, you know!!!!!!". So they want a fantasy movie. So we can ask: "Sure! Are you looking for a fantasy movie?
